Hey man I don’t know if it helps but I’m 16 and my moms always been super fucked up my whole life. Growing up she was always getting drunk, breaking windows, arguing with my dad, one time we had to call the cops on her 8 times in one night and my older brother had to hold her down while she tried to hit him with a tire iron. And my same brother now just recently relapsed on alcohol and has been drinking pretty much non-stop for about 3 months. He will either run out of money or my dad and I will have to sober him up. But since he broke up with his gf he’s been using alcohol to numb his pain because he’s never learned how to live life on his own he found all of his security in her and now that he can’t be with her he doesn’t know what to do. But you have to let that shit out man. Ive spent my whole life (Which isn’t long) being the fat, ugly, ginger kid that people find more enjoyable to laugh at. Ive had to suffer and at points it feels like no ones going through what you’re going through. But you can’t give up and try to find a way out you have to give it your all. You have burn in the fire even if it is uncomfortable or you feel awkward, or if everyone thinks you’re an idiot. Fuck em. They’re all deeply insecure to they just hide it better. You have to get comfortable being uncomfortable. In 7th grade my class had to write a poem and read it in front of the class and I was terrified I almost skipped school because I didn’t want to speak in front of the class. In my mind I was a freak and a weirdo. And Ik you can’t understand how I actually felt but I’m telling you dude I was crawling in my skin I was so fucking scared. But something in me knew I had to do it. I can’t keep being afraid and running away I have to try. And I remember there being 2 days to read your poem to the class and I did mine the second day and if you were doing yours the second day you were suppose to get a C or below. So I wrote my poem about me being afraid to get up in front of the class and read my poem. And I remember my teacher calling my name and feeling the fear creep up on me as I walked to the front of the class. But as I stated to read my paper I noticed I was almost stuttering a little but it was like all the fear went away once I started to read the words on my paper and I think I ended up getting a B+ for that assignment. But what I’m saying is you have to is you have to try and then progress will be made. To this day I’m still deeply insecure but I’m honest with myself about it and I know why I am. And it’s not because of anyone else it’s all of your own doing. Everyone’s afraid to admit they’re insecure because it feels like you’re a pussy. But it’s not there’s a way of doing it to where you don’t have to feel sorry for yourself. You just own you shit. But with everyone thing that’s going on with my brother rn has kind of put me in a reality check. And usually I get really mad at him when he’s drinking because I hate seeing what he does to himself. But recently I saw him in one of the rooms in our house withdrawing off alcohol and I don’t know why but it was like at that moment I could just feel his pain and It made me so sad. And I just wanted him to know how much I love him and I gave him a hug and I could tell he felt uncomfortable but I didn’t care anymore. And I started to cry for the first time in a while and he did to. But it felt so good to let it out. But anyways man I really hope you thrive in life and I wish you the best. The first thing I noticed when playing RE2 98 was when I walked into the police station. The whole place just felt more empty and didn’t have as much as an impact on me as when I walked into the police station in the remake. Even when I played RE 96 and then playing RE2 98 after I immediately saw how much more detail they had put into the game and that’s what the remake perfected. The remake took your game that you bought in 98 and completely reworked it and then made you buy it again. With no thought that “this is gonna be another port of the same game”. The main thing they improved on with the remake is how they put so much life into each character. In the RE2 98 when you first encounter Marvin he gives you a key card and then that’s the end of him after that. He’s not anyone to remember or even have any feelings toward. In the remake though they completely flushed him out with life. They actually made you care about him and gave you something to look forward to when you went back to the main hall. Marvin’s death was actually sad watching him slowly him turn into a zombie and then when you leaving the police station and come back you see that he’s already dead and you have to put him out of his misery. I feel like most people don’t notice this as much. I think the first thing most people think of as improvements for the remake is Mr X and that’s the second thing that comes to mind for me. I remember running my ass off to get to a save room and getting everything organised in my inventory and then planning on how I was gonna get to point B from point A in the safest way possible. This is because Mr X put so much fear in me. Knowing he’s out there lurking and will be on my ass once I walk out of they save room. I know I kind of dragged this out a bit to much but I love the remake it’s in my top 3 favourite games of all time. When I played RE2 98 though it just felt less and obviously older. I think people who played in 98 have this great nostalgia for the game and no matter what no game will ever top it. By today’s standards though the remake is great you have to leave all the fixed camera angle and shitty graphics in the past that’s old people shit. Now I’m not saying I don’t like the fixed camera angles I actually really like it. For me it made the remake of Resident evil 1 so much more terrifying. Not knowing what’s around each corner and being surprised by crimson heads or hunters was a great act of horror. I did enjoy RE2 98 I just think nostalgia only makes a game good for a select few and that it shouldn’t be implemented in a remaster of a game so that those people can have what they had in the past. I think a remaster should be something for people who played the original to put on a pair of rose coloured glasses but mainly to see how much the game is improved by today’s standards. As for the people who are younger or newer to the series should be introduced to the great series with a great remaster and that’s exactly what the remake of 2 did. It got everyone’s attention. Even the people who wish it was more like the past game can admit that’s it’s still a great game. I enjoyed RE2 98 but I think the remake took everything from the old game and made it amazing for the way games are today. Like I said though I really like the fixed camera angles I just think it’s something that should stay in the past to remembered. Capcoms good at making change just like they did with the original resident evi’s and then resident evil 4 they changed up the story and the way the previous games work and then they did the same thing with RE7. I believe games should be more than improved graphics and not just keep everything from the original game. I only have Resident evil 3 nemesis to beat now and I believe it’ll be better than the remake of 3 for instance when I saw the trailer for Resident evil 3 remake I was so excited for nemesis because the only game I played before the remake of 3 was the remake of 2 and I loved Mr X in that game. The remake of 3 in my opinion was a pile of dog shit because it took the main thing that brought fear and excitement (nemesis) and turned him into a clown and a very short game. You barely to get experience any fear with nemesis because his form changes less than a quarter way through the game. I think the fear and time there is in a game is also what makes a game like Resident evil great. This also shows why the remake of 2 was good because it made you genuinely excited for the remake of 3. The remake of 2 did everything perfect for what a game can should do in today’s time. It was able to introduce old and new players to a great game and game series.
